name: Scope the fit-out
intro: Answer these before a single object is placed. Every answer decides which steps of the pipeline run and what the build script emits — nothing here is a preference. Leave a question blank and the run uses the documented default and says so in the report.

sections.title: Anything else

questions.note: one per line, e.g. 'BED 2 = single bed, no wardrobe' or 'KITCHEN = 600 anti-skid, counter on the north wall'

questions.ask: Anything about this plan I should know?

flags.says: A minimal brief and a cornice at every wall head are pulling in opposite directions.
flags.resolution: Drop the cornice, or pick the classical style, which is what a cornice belongs to.

flags.says: You have asked for a shadow gap at the wall base and for tile skirting. A shadow gap IS the skirting detail — stacking them gives a 12 mm reveal above a 76 mm tile and reads as a modelling error.
flags.resolution: Pick one: shadow gap, or skirting in tile.

flags.says: A photographic lighting brief usually leans on a cove, and there is no false ceiling to put one in.
flags.resolution: Allow the perimeter band, or accept that the accent layer will be surface-mounted track only.

flags.says: The render kit is on but no cameras were asked for, so nothing can be shot without adding one by hand later.
flags.resolution: Ask for at least one hero camera per room worth shooting.

flags.says: Timber plank is the main floor finish. Bathrooms, balconies and utility rooms will still be tiled — timber is not used in a wet room whatever the brief says.
flags.resolution: Nothing to do; this is a note so the per-room schedule does not surprise you.

flags.says: A builder-finish brief with photographic lighting will produce a plan whose lighting costs more than its joinery.
flags.resolution: Either lift the style, or drop the lighting to layered.
